issues.title: Epic: Foundations
issues.body:
The platform everything else builds on: repository, local development, CI, Azure infrastructure, API skeleton, data model, iOS skeleton, sign-in, languages, activity log, knowledge base pipeline, shared services (weather, media, notifications, background worker, AI layer, search) and account deletion and export. Offline sync is a good-to-have feature built on top of a data model designed for it from day one.

**Plan:** PLAN.md §2, §4, §5

**Features:** 19 MVP, 1 Good to have
**Estimated effort:** 325 h (scheduled features)

<!-- backlog-key: E00 -->

issues.title: Repository structure and .NET solution
issues.body:
**User story:** As the developer, I want a clean repository layout and .NET solution so that backend, apps, content and infrastructure each have a clear home.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Repo has backend/, ios/, android/, content/, infra/, docs/ folders as in PLAN.md §5
- [ ] .NET solution builds with Api, Domain, Infrastructure, Worker and test projects
- [ ] README explains how to build and run each part
- [ ] Code style rules (.editorconfig) are enforced on build

**Release tier:** MVP
**Estimated effort:** 11 h across 5 tasks (includes testing)
**Sprints:** Sprint 01
**Plan:** PLAN.md §2, §4, §5 · row X.E00.1

issues.title: Azure infrastructure and deployment

- [ ] A GitHub Actions pipeline deploys the API on merge to master
- [ ] Secrets live in Key Vault and are accessed with managed identity

issues.title: Core data model ready for offline sync
issues.body:
**User story:** As the developer, I want every record to have a client-generated ID and a server version so that offline sync can be added later without migrating data.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] All entities use UUIDs that the client can generate
- [ ] Every editable record has a server version number and updated timestamp
- [ ] Deletes are soft deletes
- [ ] Every record belongs to a user (multi-user from day one)
- [ ] A base entity and conventions are reused by all features

issues.title: Knowledge base schema for crops and tools
issues.body:
**User story:** As the developer, I want a well-defined structure for crop and tool data so that the calendar, planner, guides and tools features share one source.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Crop schema covers temperature thresholds, frost and heat tolerance, days to maturity, rotation family, spacing, watering guidance by season, varieties and day length

- [ ] All text fields are translatable (pt-PT and en)

issues.title: Epic: Project roadmap
issues.body:
The dynamic backbone of the app: for each zone it works out the current stage from the activity log and produces the next actions, using fixed agronomy rules and safety limits, adapted to the season, the starting point and any deviations the user reports.

**Plan:** PLAN.md §3.1

**Features:** 5 MVP, 2 Future improvement, 1 Good to have
**Estimated effort:** 122 h (scheduled features)

<!-- backlog-key: E02 -->

issues.title: Next actions (rules)
issues.body:
**User story:** As a beginner gardener, I want the app to tell me the next actions for each zone so that I always know what to do next without planning it myself.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Given a zone with a known state, when the roadmap is recalculated, then a short list of next actions is produced, each with a reason, time window, guide link and tools needed
- [ ] Safety rules are never broken (e.g. no transplanting frost-sensitive crops while there is frost risk)
- [ ] Recalculation runs when a relevant activity log entry is added and once a day
- [ ] Each recommendation stores the knowledge-base version that produced it
- [ ] The latest next actions are shown in the app

**Release tier:** MVP
**Estimated effort:** 49 h across 11 tasks (includes testing)
**Sprints:** Sprint 05, Sprint 06
**Depends on:** Activity log; Knowledge base pipeline; API skeleton; Per-zone stages
**Plan:** PLAN.md §3.1 · row 3.1.1

issues.title: Epic: Planting calendar
issues.body:
A climate-driven calendar that tells the user what to sow or plant out, and when, for their exact location. Windows come from crop temperature rules applied to local climate history, avoid both frost and excessive heat, and adjust to the forecast.

issues.title: Climate-based windows
issues.body:

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Given a plot location, the app shows direct-sow, plant-out and harvest windows for each catalog crop
- [ ] Windows come from crop temperature rules applied to 30 years of local climate history, not fixed months
- [ ] Changing the plot location recalculates the windows
- [ ] Calculation runs on the server with fixed rules (no AI) and results are cached per plot
- [ ] Windows for Alentejo match a reference regional sowing calendar within about 2 weeks for 10 sample crops

**Release tier:** MVP
**Estimated effort:** 34 h across 9 tasks (includes testing)
**Sprints:** Sprint 03, Sprint 04

issues.title: Week planner
issues.body:
**User story:** As a gardener with limited time, I want to set the hours I have on each day of next week and get the important tasks spread across them, so that I use my time well and see it in my calendar.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] I set hours per day for next week (Mon–Sun), with "Same as last week" and a one-tap "Day off" per day
- [ ] The app spreads tasks across the days by window, weather, size, priority and order dependencies
- [ ] I can accept the plan, which schedules each task on its day
- [ ] A Monday reminder asks me to plan next week, and a "Plan next week" card on Today turns green (Mon–Wed), amber (Thu–Fri) and orange (Sat–Sun) until it is planned
- [ ] Planned tasks are written to a separate "Garden" calendar on the phone and kept in sync; the app never reads my calendar

**Release tier:** MVP
**Estimated effort:** 28 h across 9 tasks (includes testing)
**Sprints:** Sprint 09

issues.body:
Everything needed before the app is sold to the public: subscriptions, data licences, expert content review, professional illustrations, and legal and store preparation. Future improvement only.

issues.title: Freemium subscriptions
issues.body:
**User story:** As the owner, I want App Store and Play subscriptions with free and premium tiers so that the app can earn money when it goes commercial.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Premium tier unlocks AI features
- [ ] Server-side receipt validation for App Store and Google Play
- [ ] Usage limits follow the tier
- [ ] Users can manage or cancel their subscription

**Release tier:** Future improvement
**Not scheduled.** Tasks will be broken down when this is planned.
**Plan:** PLAN.md §6 M7, §7 · row 7.1

<!-- backlog-key: E20/7.1 -->

issues.title: Commercial data licences
issues.body:
**User story:** As the owner, I want commercial licences for all data sources so that the app can legally be sold.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Open-Meteo paid plan or an alternative weather provider in place
- [ ] IPMA and MeteoAlarm reuse terms checked
- [ ] SoilGrids attribution shown
- [ ] Any plant-ID service licensed for commercial use

**Release tier:** Future improvement
**Not scheduled.** Tasks will be broken down when this is planned.
**Plan:** PLAN.md §6 M7, §7 · row 7.2

<!-- backlog-key: E20/7.2 -->

issues.title: Expert review of guides
issues.body:
**User story:** As the owner, I want an agronomist to review all guides so that the advice is correct before selling the app.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Every guide reviewed by a qualified expert
- [ ] Review date and reviewer recorded on each guide
- [ ] Corrections merged through the content pipeline

**Release tier:** Future improvement
**Not scheduled.** Tasks will be broken down when this is planned.
**Plan:** PLAN.md §6 M7, §7 · row 7.3

- [ ] Key guides and tools illustrated
- [ ] Images licensed for commercial use

**Release tier:** Future improvement

issues.title: Privacy policy, GDPR, store listings
issues.body:
**User story:** As the owner, I want the legal and store preparation done so that the app can be published publicly.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Privacy policy and terms published
- [ ] GDPR review completed (data processing, retention, consent)
- [ ] AI disclaimers shown, especially around chemicals
- [ ] App Store and Google Play listings with screenshots in pt-PT and en
